behind_the_work.en: Dialogue of the Wind began as a magazine cover. In 2007 Lai and a colleague from the dancers' association planned a year of covers for Ballet, China's first periodical devoted to the form, each built around a sculpture; this one became "dancing time and space". Two dancers twist and stretch through each other — masculine force against feminine softness, flowing form against opened space. Lai wanted the fleeting instant without copying a photograph; his note recalls a line from the Chu Ci's "Mountain Spirit" and names Bernini and Maillol as the masters he had in mind. The archive records the first version in stainless steel.
behind_the_work.zh: 《風之對話》起於一組封面。2007年，賴錫康與舞協友人為中國第一本芭蕾專刊《芭蕾》設計全年封面，以雕塑為載體：精靈的起舞《金色的時代》、舞動的時空《風之對話》、排練場的艱辛《釋》、舞蹈人的驕傲《舞者》。作品塑造一對扭動伸展的舞者——雄性的強悍與雌性的柔美，流動的形體與解構的空間。他要抓住稍縱即逝的瞬間，卻刻意避免複製照片；創作筆記引《楚辭．山鬼》「表獨立兮山之上，雲容容兮而在下」，並自述向貝尼尼與馬約爾致敬。檔案記載原作為不鏽鋼。
src: Archive (Conlin 2) 1/P8: artist's note, Oct 2009, and work record
Bilingual work notes, Dialogue of the Wind (2014 file)
2025 catalogue, pp. 25–26
open: The work record lists Ballet 2007, vol. 2; the artist's note speaks of the magazine's third issue.
作品紀錄載《芭蕾》2007年第2期；創作筆記則稱為第三期封面。
The colleague is named in the note only as 舞協小憬先生.
筆記中僅稱合作者為「舞協小憬先生」。

quote.zh: 雕塑家的價值在於表現出那瞬間美的神韻。
quote.en: The sculptor's worth lies in conveying the spirit of that instant of beauty.

behind_the_work.en: A chance visit to a yoga practice gave Lai this figure. He was struck by how far a body could bend and still flow, and saw in the backbend an arch — an "inverted arch" that a bridge achieves only with difficulty and a person only beyond the limit. For him the pose held a paradox: stretched to the extreme, the body curves; curved to the extreme, it stretches. His note turns to the Daodejing — "being and non-being give rise to each other", "what is bent becomes whole" — as the inner law of things. Carved in white marble, the arch is at once structure and breath.
behind_the_work.zh: 一次偶然觀看瑜伽練習，賴錫康為人體的柔韌與舒展所折服。他在背弓的姿態裡看見一座拱橋——「倒拱」：橋造成這樣已屬不易，人做到這樣，卻是越過極限、又舒展到極點。曲與伸在此互為因果；他由此想到《道德經》「有無相生，難易相成」與「曲則全，枉則正」，視之為萬物的內在關係。漢白玉讓這道弧線同時是結構，也是呼吸。
src: Archive (Conlin 2) 3/P26: artist's note, 29 Oct 2010
Bilingual work notes, 曲伸之美 (2014 file)
2025 catalogue, pp. 27–28
open: The archive's English title is Stretching to the Extreme; the site follows the catalogue.
檔案英文題名為 Stretching to the Extreme；本站依畫冊題名。

quote.zh: 這是伸極而曲，或是曲極而伸吧。
quote.en: Stretched to the extreme, it curves — or curved to the extreme, it stretches.

note: Catalogue English title: The Human Body Lying on Its Side

behind_the_work.en: Midsummer Night grew out of a heatwave. Lai read of university students in one of China's "furnace" cities who, with no air-conditioning, carried their bedding onto the roof to sleep in the wind. The images brought two unrelated works to mind — Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream and the film Life Is Beautiful — and with them the thought that people meet misfortune with optimism rather than complaint. He deconstructed the figure into a pose no real body holds, "a contradiction of compression and opening", and anticipated that some would find it excessive. The Beijing writer Chen Yuan, its first viewer, saw not a delicate nude but a female body with strength within its charm.
behind_the_work.zh: 《仲夏夜》源於一個特別早、也特別熱的夏天。賴錫康讀到報道：「火爐」城市的大學生在沒有空調的夜裡捲起鋪蓋，跑到樓頂與風對話。他腦海中竟同時浮現莎士比亞的《仲夏夜》與電影《美麗人生》——命運總把人和事安排得陰差陽錯，正因如此才有了故事。他以解構的方式，把現實中不存在的動態構造成「擠壓與開發的矛盾體」，也坦言或有人覺得動態過了。北京作家陳援是此作的第一位讀者，他看到的不是纖柔婀娜的女人體，而是「嫵媚中也有力度的女性身軀」。

Chen Yuan, "On reading Midsummer Night", 28 Nov 2015 (same folder)
2025 catalogue, pp. 31–32
open: The note, written in November 2015, places the heatwave in the previous early summer; the work is dated 2015.
筆記寫於2015年11月，稱熱浪發生於「去年的初夏」；作品年份記為2015。

quote.zh: 或許您會從我的這件雕塑中體味到去年仲夏的那個夜晚——人與自然的對話。
quote.en: Perhaps in this sculpture you will taste that midsummer night of last year — a dialogue between people and nature.

title_en: An Eagle Flying in the Night Sky of the City
source: Artist archive (Conlin 2): 2/P15 and bilingual work notes

behind_the_work.en: Lai paired this figure with a short prose poem, dated April 2010. It looks down on a city at night: neon breaking like surf over a forest of steel and concrete, roads like a spider's web along which prosperity flows and then abruptly stops, joy and sorrow, noise and loneliness. In that sky a dancer moves — "the lone eagle of the city's night" — who wants to throw off the rising heat and recover a free spirit, and a free city. The cupronickel body, all upward reach, is the poem's single image.
behind_the_work.zh: 賴錫康為這件作品寫了一首短詩，署於2010年4月。詩從夜空俯瞰城市：霓虹燈璀璨的浪花翻滾在鋼筋混凝土的森林，蛛網一樣的道路任繁華與榮耀流淌，時而又戛然而止；有歡樂也有哀愁，有喧囂也有寂寞。夜空中一位舞者翩翩起舞——「這都市夜空裡孤獨的鷹」，要掙脫熱浪，找回自由的精神與自由的城市。白銅人體向上伸展，正是詩中唯一的意象。
src: Bilingual work notes, 城市夜空的鷹 (2012/2014 files)

quote.zh: 她要掙脫這熱浪找回那自由的精神，
quote.en: She wants to break free of this heat and find again that free spirit,

note: Year and material differ between archive sources (2010, cupronickel / 2011, bronze)
source: Artist archive (Conlin 2): 1/P11 and bilingual work notes

behind_the_work.en: Lai answered this figure with a poem of his own, dated 23 April 2011 and written in Chinese with his own English version. It moves between the two poles of the title: an eagle rising straight into the clouds, a drop of spring water throwing itself to the ground to feel the earth's broad heart. The speaker opens his arms to the world, stands upright between the vast sky and the boundless wilderness, and looks for an ideal country where happiness replaces hardship, fairness replaces injustice, and truth replaces absurdity. The dancer's long vertical line is drawn between those two poles.
behind_the_work.zh: 賴錫康以一首自作的詩回應這件作品，署於2011年4月23日，並附自譯英文。詩在題目的兩極之間往返：雄鷹直上雲天，在無邊的天際翱翔；甘泉撲向大地，感受泥土寬廣的胸懷。詩人敞開心扉、展開雙臂，挺立在遼闊的蒼穹與無邊的曠野，尋找理想的國度——用幸福代替苦難，用公正代替不平，用真理代替荒謬。舞者修長的垂直線，正拉在天與地之間。
src: Archive (Conlin 2) 1/P12: poem, 23 Apr 2011
Bilingual work notes, 天與地 (2014 file)
open: The archive records an appearance on the cover of Dance Study vol. 114 (2007), earlier than the work's recorded date of 2011; year and material also differ between files.
檔案記載此作曾刊於《舞蹈研究》2007年第114期封面，早於記錄的2011年；年份與材質各檔案亦不一。

quote.zh: 如果我是一隻雄鷹，我要直上雲天，在那無邊的天際翱翔。
quote.en: If I was an eagle / I would fly / fly high up in the sky

behind_the_work.en: Lai's note on Balance begins with fear. Years ago, near a mountain summit, he and his friends had to recross a narrow stone bridge as storm clouds closed in; some hurried, some all but crawled, and halfway over he felt his heart leave his body and fall. Against that memory he set lighter ones — walking kerbs and parking rails with children who laughed at every wobble — and the slow control of yoga, in which he sensed a strength "no less than Muhammad Ali's". The cupronickel figure holds that tension at rest. The design received the Excellence Award for Sculpture Design for the 16th Asian Games (Guangzhou, 2010).
behind_the_work.zh: 賴錫康談《平衡》，先從恐懼說起。多年前他與友人登山，峰頂附近一座石板橋連結兩峰；風雲驟至，眾人站上橋頭便發暈，有人快步走過，有人幾乎是爬過去的。他只記得走到中間時，「心好像已經離開了身體掉到橋下去了」。與之相對的，是陪孩子走護欄、花基的樂趣，以及瑜伽在舒緩節奏中達到的平衡——他從中感到的力量「不亞於拳王阿里」。白銅人體把這份張力凝定為靜。此設計獲第十六屆亞洲運動會（2010，廣州）雕塑設計優秀獎。
src: Archive (Conlin 2) 2/P14: artist's notes (draft and May 2012 version)
Bilingual work notes, 平衡 (2014 file)
2025 catalogue, p. 34; artist CV
open: The note names the mountain as 南岳恒山, which conflates two different peaks (Nanyue is Mount Heng 衡山); the site does not name it.
筆記稱「南岳恒山」，南嶽應為衡山，與北嶽恒山相混，故本站不列山名。

quote.zh: 只有平靜的內心才會生起智慧，並滋養出無懼和力量。
quote.en: Only a calm mind gives rise to wisdom, and nourishes fearlessness and strength.

behind_the_work.en: Filed with this work in the artist's archive is a single line from Shelley's "Ode to the West Wind": "If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?" The title's two seasons, joined by a single dot, hold that turn from one to the other.
behind_the_work.zh: 藝術家檔案中與此作同存的，只有雪萊〈西風頌〉的一句詩：「If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?」（冬天來了，春天還會遠嗎？）。題名中的兩個季節以一點相連，正是由此及彼的轉折。
src: Archive (Conlin 2) 2/P18: 雪萊的詩：西風

behind_the_work.en: Resultant Force is a low, horizontal surge of torn, wind-swept forms in cast iron, every edge driven the same way — a sum of forces rather than a single body. Its record spans a decade: sold at Huayi International's autumn auction in 2017, it was shown at the Taichung Cross-Strait Sculpture Exhibition in 2018 and again at the Taichung International Invitational in 2025. Filed with it in the artist's archive is a classical-style poem, "Song of the Wild Horse" by Gao Xuhong, written in Yanji in the winter of 1998; the archive does not say how the poem relates to the sculpture.
behind_the_work.zh: 《合力》以鑄鐵塑造一股低伏、橫向奔湧的力量：撕裂而迎風的形體，每一道邊緣都朝同一方向推進——是諸力之和，而非單一的身體。作品的紀錄跨越十年：2017年於華藝國際秋拍成交，2018年參加臺中兩岸雕塑展，2025年再度參加臺中國際邀請展。藝術家檔案中與之同存的，是高旭紅1998年冬作於吉林延吉的古體詩〈野馬歌〉；檔案未說明此詩與作品的關係。

Archive (Conlin 2) 2/P20: "Song of the Wild Horse" (Gao Xuhong, 1998)

behind_the_work.en: Float is the one series the 2025 catalogue introduces with an essay. The Beijing Evening News columnist Chen Yuan described the first Float as a woman's body head-down, folded back almost ninety degrees at the waist, her swept-back hair and one outstretched leg nearly parallel — limbs that show "not softness, but the strength of the tendons". He recalled the old saying that woman is like water, and a Mongolian song praising the father as the sky, and wondered whether Lai had fused the two. A decade later, Float (Part 3) draws the same horizontal line out to 95 centimetres, carried over a rounded, wave-lined base.
behind_the_work.zh: 「水天」是2025年畫冊中唯一附有專文的系列。《北京晚報》專欄作家陳援從北京寫道：第一件《水天》是一個頭部向下、腰以下幾近九十度後折的女性人體，後掠的長髮與向後平伸的腿幾成平行；修長的肢體表現的「不是婀娜柔潤，而是肌腱的力度」。他想起「女人如水」之說與蒙古族「父親如天」的頌歌，揣想錫康是否把兩層寓意融匯為一。十年後，《水天（之三）》把同一道水平線拉長至95公分，承托於一個刻有波紋的圓形基座之上。

quote.en: The slender limbs express not softness and grace, but the strength of the tendons.

behind_the_work.en: Civilized Ruins was Lai's graduation work at the Guangzhou Academy of Fine Arts in 1990: an arched, crumbling wall carrying the marks of civilisation — oracle-bone script, a line of Shakespeare — beneath a warrior's helmet, with pigeons standing on the ruin like sentries and a curved stainless-steel base sharpening the contrast. A review in Guangdong Youth Daily (9 September 1992) read it as a work of "contemplation and questioning", and noted that the face beneath the helmet, present in the clay sketch, had been hollowed out on the advice of professionals — a change the reviewers regretted. In 2022 Lai returned to the form in bronze; the 2025 catalogue titles it Ruins — Gate of Peace, the first of the Gate series.
behind_the_work.zh: 《廢墟》是賴錫康1990年在廣州美術學院的畢業創作：一道拱形頹牆印滿文明進程的轍痕——甲骨文、莎士比亞的名句——上方是武士的頭盔，鴿子在廢墟上走動、佇立如哨兵，不鏽鋼弧形底座更使質感與時代的反差分明。1992年9月9日《廣東青年報》的評論稱之為「默思與追詢」，並指出泥稿中頭盔下原有一副默思的面容，定稿依專業人士建議把臉挖去——評者對此深感可惜。2022年，賴錫康以青銅重回此作；2025年畫冊題為《廢墟—和平之門》，列為「門系列之一」。
src: Archive (Conlin 2): work notes 文明的廢墟 (2012/2014 files), reprinting the 1992 review
2025 catalogue, pp. 4–6
open: The 1990 dimensions differ: 280 × 150 × 230 cm (catalogue, Chinese) and 250 × 320 cm (catalogue and archive, English).
1990年版尺寸記載不一：280×150×230cm（畫冊中文）與250×320cm（畫冊及檔案英文）。
The review is signed 公明 in one archive file; that this is Li Gongming of the Academy is likely but unconfirmed.
評論在檔案中署名「公明」，是否即廣州美術學院李公明教授，尚待確認。
The archive's Chinese title is 文明的廢墟; the catalogue uses 廢墟.
檔案中文題名為《文明的廢墟》，畫冊作《廢墟》。

quote.zh: 在文明的廢墟上反思歷史。
quote.en: To reflect on history upon the ruins of civilisation.

A review in Guangdong Youth Daily (9 September 1992) read it as a work of "contemplation and questioning", and noted that the face beneath the helmet, present in the clay sketch, had been hollowed out on the advice of professionals — a change the reviewers regretted. behind_the_work.zh: 《廢墟》是賴錫康1990年在廣州美術學院的畢業創作：一道拱形頹牆印滿文明進程的轍痕——甲骨文、莎士比亞的名句——上方是武士的頭盔，鴿子在廢墟上走動、佇立如哨兵，不鏽鋼弧形底座更使質感與時代的反差分明。1992年9月9日《廣東青年報》的評論稱之為「默思與追詢」，並指出泥稿中頭盔下原有一副默思的面容，定稿依專業人士建議把臉挖去——評者對此深感可惜。2022年，賴錫康以青銅重回此作；2025年畫冊題為《廢墟—和平之門》，列為「門系列之一」。

quote.zh: 在文明的廢墟上反思歷史。
quote.en: To reflect on history upon the ruins of civilisation.

title_en: The Gate of Spirit (Gate Series II)

behind_the_work.en: The Gate series turns the arch of Civilized Ruins into geometry. Where the 1990 gate was a weathered wall beneath a helmet, the later gates are built from interlocking, hollowed blocks that tilt and shift against their bases, opening voids through their own mass. The 2025 catalogue numbers them as one sequence — Gate of Peace, Gate of Spirit, Gate of Awakening, Gate of Chaos — and sets the later gates beside the small bronze maquettes from which they grew, so the series reads as thinking in steps: a gate first held in the hand, then realised in steel. The titles move from a public hope to inner states; the forms move from ruin to construction.
behind_the_work.zh: 「門系列」把《廢墟》的拱門化為幾何。1990年的門是頭盔下一道風化的牆；其後的門則由相互咬合、中空的方塊構成，在底座上傾斜錯動，於自身體量中打開虛空。2025年畫冊把它們編為同一序列——和平之門、意志之門、覺醒之門、混沌之門——並把後來的門與其青銅小稿並置：一道門先握在手中，再以鋼材實現。題名由公共的祈願轉向內在的狀態；形式則由廢墟走向構築。

behind_the_work.en: Lai received this commission on 20 August and began reading An Jung-geun's story in an airport departure lounge. At the unveiling — held with the assembly marking the centenary of An's act — he said he had tried to understand the history "bit by bit" and to shape "a warrior like a meteor" through symbol, movement and freedom from detail. The writer Chen Yuan noted that Lai chose An's resolute bearing rather than the familiar moment of the shooting. The figure stands in the An Jung-geun Memorial Hall in Harbin.
behind_the_work.zh: 賴錫康8月20日接到這件工作，坐在機場候機大廳裡開始閱讀安重根的故事。在揭幕暨紀念安重根義舉一百周年大會上，他說自己盡量去了解歷史的點點滴滴，試圖讀懂他，期望以符號、動感和不拘細節的手法，塑造「流星一般的勇士」。作家陳援指出，他沒有表現一般藝術家常選的開槍瞬間，而選擇了英雄義無反顧的姿態。塑像立於哈爾濱安重根紀念館。
src: Archive (Conlin 2): work notes 安重根紀念像 (2012 file), with the unveiling address and Chen Yuan's letter
open: Date and height differ across sources: archive files give 2000 (H 220 cm) and February 2010 (H 270 cm); the CV gives 2009 (H 190 cm). The centenary of An's act fell in October 2009.
年份與高度各檔案不一：2000年（H220cm）、2010年2月（H270cm）；簡歷作2009年（H190cm）。安重根義舉一百周年為2009年10月。

quote.zh: 我期望以符號、動感和不拘細節的表現手法塑造流星一般的勇士。
quote.en: I hoped to shape a warrior like a meteor, through symbol, movement and a manner unbound by detail.

Archive English title: In the Sake of Peace
source: Artist archive (Conlin 2): 4/P39, work notes and the artist's 2011 address

behind_the_work.en: For Peace is a bronze relief 9.5 metres long for the An Jung-geun Memorial Hall in Harbin. Speaking there in October 2011, Lai said he had borrowed from painting: a dramatic scene at the centre, held in balance by horizontal lines running to either end — on the left the mountains and sea of An's homeland, on the right the newspapers that reported his act and his declaration of peace, with stacked blocks and a train suggesting time folding into space. The relief's irregular outline is a geometric echo of the map of Korea, carrying, in his words, a hope for its unification. He closed with a plea for different nations and peoples to live side by side in peace.
behind_the_work.zh: 《為了和平》是哈爾濱安重根紀念館的青銅浮雕，長9.5米。2011年10月，賴錫康在館內演講時說，他借用了繪畫的元素：中心再現戲劇性的場景，以橫線連接兩端、控制不規則構圖的平衡——左邊是象徵義士故鄉的山與海，右邊是舉義後的各大報紙與擲地有聲的和平宣言，多重方塊與列車相連，產生時空交積之感。浮雕不規則的外形取自幾何化的大韓版圖，寄託統一的美好願望。他最後說：和平來之不易，自由更是珍貴。
src: Archive (Conlin 2) 4/P39: the artist's address, 25 Oct 2011
Bilingual work notes, 為了和平——義士安重根 (2014 file)

quote.zh: 回顧歷史珍惜和平是我的創作目的。
quote.en: Looking back on history and cherishing peace is the purpose of my work.
